company_context: Apex Group — Global Fund Solutions Division (synthetic demo entity). A single-source, global fund administrator and asset servicer operating across 50+ jurisdictions, providing fund administration, private-markets servicing, depositary, custody, corporate services, and ManCo/ESG solutions to alternative and institutional managers. The division administers c.$3.5 trillion in assets under administration (AUA) across roughly 13,200 FTEs. FY runs July–June; these figures reflect FY26 (Jul-2025 to Jun-2026) full-year run and the board pack for the June 2026 close. The business is fee-based and largely recurring, with revenue driven by NAV/AUA-linked ad-valorem fees, per-transaction and per-entity charges, and project/onboarding work. Growth is led by private equity and real-assets servicing and by ESG/ManCo mandates; the demo is calibrated to look credible to a CFO's deputy reviewing monthly actuals vs budget vs forecast.

variance_commentary.commentary: Full-year revenue landed marginally below plan, driven almost entirely by the June close. Recurring AUA-linked fees tracked budget through Q3; the shortfall is timing, not run-rate erosion, and reverses in early FY27 as delayed closes complete.

Standout performer, ahead of both budget and prior year on strong fund launches and drawdown activity across three anchor GP relationships. Onboarding-related project fees pulled forward c.$8M into H1; underlying recurring growth remains double-digit.

Two large private-markets onboardings slipped past 30-June due to client-side legal delays, and a NAV-strike timing shift deferred c.$6M of ad-valorem fees. No mandates were lost; c.$14M is expected to recognise in July–August.

Margin expansion despite headcount growth, reflecting platform automation in fund accounting and a favourable shift in mix toward higher-margin ManCo/ESG and PE servicing. Wage inflation was largely offset by improved offshore utilisation.

Collections discipline and earlier invoicing on project work reduced DSO to 52 days, releasing c.$21M of working capital in the quarter. Aged receivables over 90 days fell to 4.1% of the book from 5.3%.

Fastest-growing segment off a small base, driven by SFDR/ESG reporting mandates and third-party AIFM/ManCo appointments in Luxembourg and Ireland. Pipeline supports sustained 20%+ growth into FY27; segment now 6.0% of revenue.
